humanities_role_explanation: History and Geography are only two of 17 general fields (Politics, Finance, Science, Health, Media). Items are structured web-retrieval and constraint-filtering tasks (e.g., Eurostat, CDC, Statistics Canada data); the competence tested is general deep-research agency, not disciplinary humanities competence. The Sherardian Library botanist example is an isolated archival-catalogue lookup.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text-only prompts and text answer sets, with agents browsing the open web.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Agents run multi-step web search to produce exhaustive answer sets (paper: 'exhaustive answer list', 'Systematic Collation', 'Entity Resolution (De-duplication)', 'Stopping Criteria'). Tasks add constraint solving and intersection of thresholds (Inference & Constraint Solving), structured retrieval, and context management. Single-answer items are close to factual recall of obscure data. Scoring is set-based precision/recall/F1.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to one task type, deep-research / exhaustive information seeking, although it spans 17 fields.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Gemini Deep Research Agent, GPT-5 Pro/High, Gemini 3 Pro Preview, o3/o4-mini Deep Research, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Claude 4.5 Opus/Sonnet/Haiku.

quantitative_metrics.note: F1 (primary), precision, recall, Fully Correct, Fully Incorrect, Correct with Extraneous Answers rates with 95% CIs.

summary: DeepSearchQA is a 900-prompt benchmark of hand-crafted multi-step information-seeking tasks across 17 fields, requiring agents to return exhaustive, verifiable answer sets from the open web. It is scored with set-based precision, recall and F1, using an LLM judge. Top agents still struggle with the recall-precision tradeoff, showing premature stopping and hedging.
key_findings: Gemini Deep Research Agent leads with F1 81.90 and 66.09% Fully Correct; GPT-5 Pro High Reasoning gets 78.98 F1 and 65.18%. Claude 4.5 Haiku is lowest at 22.24 F1. Deep research agents outperform standalone reasoning models. About a 15-point gap separates F1 from Fully Correct. Sampling n=8 raises Fully Correct from 67.18% to 85.71%.
facets_explanation: Questions were curated by expert data annotators and verified by a three-phase protocol (independent research, comparison, conflict resolution). Ambiguous prompts were filtered out, which treats disagreement as noise. These annotators are described as expert data annotators, not humanities specialists; the paper does not state their disciplinary training. Answers require web research beyond the prompt, and scoring accepts a ground-truth set of items.
results_explanation: Table 4 gives Gemini Deep Research Agent 'F1 81.90' and Fully Correct 66.09 ±3.16. The paper notes 'This roughly 15-point gap' between F1 (81.90%) and strict success (66.09%), a scoring-rule gap. It also reports more test-time compute raising Fully Correct 'from 67.18% (n = 1) to 85.71% (n = 8)', an input/compute comparison of smaller size (~18 points, not taken as the largest because the scoring gap is labeled kind scoring; the sampling gap is actually larger at 18.5 points, so the stated 15 understates the largest). No human baseline is reported.
